claim.why_it_matters: The whole right column loses the index hierarchy: sub-entries print at the same level as headwords. The index is informative, but a flattened or merged index entry misattributes page references to the wrong headword.

verdict.reasoning: Rendered page 930 (printed 906, index B/C). In the PDF's right column, sub-entries are visibly indented under their headwords: National 17 / Numeric 18 continue the Character sub-list from the left column; OBJECT-COMPUTER paragraph 228 is under CHARACTER CLASSIFICATION clause 229; ALLOCATE/BLOCK CONTAINS/INSPECT/RECORD under CHARACTERS phrase; BASE 735 / Parameterized 200 under Class; SPECIAL-NAMES 231 under CLASS clause; BOOLEAN phrase under Class condition; Alphanumeric..Pointer 129 under Class of data; USAGE clause under CLASS phrase; CLASS clause..Truth value under Class-name; Implied under CLOSE statement; Report description entry under CODE clause; SPECIAL-NAMES 232 under Code-name. The markdown gives every right-column line the same 3-space prefix with no   marker (the left column uses   for sub-entries), so headwords and sub-entries are at one level and e.g. 'BASE 735' or 'OBJECT-COMPUTER paragraph 228' read as independent headwords. The claim quotes both sources accurately. This is more than whitespace: in an index the nesting carries which headword a page reference belongs to, so the meaning of entries changes. Informative annex content only, so structural not normative.
